```{r setup, message=FALSE}
source("00_requirements.R")
load("12_DataSaving.RData")

```

```{r}
nfl_data <- read.csv("candidates_21-25.csv")
index_21 <- (nfl_data$season == 2021)
index_22 <- (nfl_data$season == 2022)
index_23 <- (nfl_data$season == 2023)
index_24 <- (nfl_data$season == 2024)
index_25 <- (nfl_data$season == 2025)
data_2021 <- nfl_data[index_21, ]
data_2022 <- nfl_data[index_22, ]
data_2023 <- nfl_data[index_23, ]
data_2024 <- nfl_data[index_24, ]
data_2025 <- nfl_data[index_25, ]
```

##Passing Yards per Season
The following graphs show the passing yards of the quarterbacks who were candidates for MVP of that specific season.
```{r}
mvp_color <- ifelse(data_2021$mvp == 1, "green", "blue")
mvp_pch <- ifelse(data_2021$mvp == 1, 19, 1)
plot(1:nrow(data_2021), data_2021$pass_yds,  xlab = "Player Candidate", ylab = "Passing Yards", main = "Passing Yards for 2021", col = mvp_color, pch = mvp_pch, cex = 2)
abline(h = data_2021$pass_yds[data_2021$mvp == 1], col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
Based on the graph above, we can see that the MVP quarterback for 2021 had a lower amount of passing yards than majority of the other candidates.

## Numerical summary: MVPs vs. other QBs
Mean of each statistic for the MVP and for the other candidates.
```{r summary}
qb |>
  group_by(mvp) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(pass_yds, pass_td, pass_int, rush_yds, win_pct, td_int_ratio),
                   ~ round(mean(.x), 2))) |>
  kable()
```
Based on the data above, we can see that the average among the 5 MVPs are better in every stat compared to the candidates.

## Boxplots of key statistics
MVPs marked as red points.
```{r boxplots}
# plot_stat_box(): boxplot of one statistic for MVP vs. other QBs.
# Input: df - QB data; stat - column name (string); label - axis label
# Output: a ggplot object
plot_stat_box <- function(df, stat, label) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = mvp, y = .data[[stat]])) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(data = filter(df, mvp == "MVP"), color = "red", width = 0.05, size = 2) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = label, title = paste(label, "by MVP status"))
}
plot_stat_box(qb, "pass_td", "Passing touchdowns")
plot_stat_box(qb, "pass_yds", "Passing yards")
plot_stat_box(qb, "pass_int", "Interceptions")
plot_stat_box(qb, "win_pct", "Team win percentage")
```
Based on the graph above, we can see that the average among MVPs are higher in passing touchdowns and team win percentage, and lower in interceptions compared to the other candidates. 

## Touchdowns vs. team success
```{r scatter}
ggplot(qb, aes(x = win_pct, y = pass_td, color = mvp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(qb, mvp == "MVP"),
                           aes(label = paste(player_name, season)), show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Team win percentage", y = "Passing touchdowns", color = NULL,
       title = "MVP QBs team wins and passing touchdowns")
```
Based on the graph above, we can see that all the MVPs in the past 5 years had a win percentage above 0.7, but passing touchdowns vary among them.

The table shows the MVP's rank on each statistic, and the plot shows the average rank
(lower = the MVP tended to lead the field on that statistic).
```{r ranks}
rank_cols <- grep("_rank$", names(qb), value = TRUE)

qb |> filter(mvp == "MVP") |> select(season, player_name, all_of(rank_cols)) |> kable()

qb |>
  filter(mvp == "MVP") |>
  summarise(across(all_of(rank_cols), mean)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "avg_rank") |>
  mutate(statistic = sub("_rank$", "", statistic)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(statistic, avg_rank), y = avg_rank)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Average within-season rank of the MVP (1 = best)",
       title = "Which statistics do MVPs lead the league in?")
```
Based on the graph above, we can see that the touchdowns per interception ratio and win percentage are the two most important statistics when it comes to deciding who the MVP is.
